title: vault: investigate persistent no-push on dev role (starving #1620, #1622, #1631)
body:
## What was reported

The `dev` agent role repeatedly fails to push branches for #1620 (and #1630): 4 consecutive exits `no_result`, `timeout`, `no_push_after_3_attempts`, `no_push_after_3_attempts`. Each failure leaves the issue `blocked`, which starves the dependent backlog issues #1622 and #1631 (both `backlog`, quality-gate-passing, otherwise-ready).

## Known context

- #1620's own dependencies (#1618, #1629) are both `closed`, so the block is **not** an unmet dependency — it is a compute/resource failure (the diagnostic line is `Resource limit (timeout) — Claude did not push branch fix/issue-1620`).
- A prior gardener run (2026-10-01 13:16) re-queued #1620 from `blocked`; it re-blocked on attempt 4 the same day. Re-queueing does not resolve it.
- #1630 shows the same `no_push` pattern.

## Reproduction plan

1. Run the `dev` organ (or let the polling loop pick the next ready backlog issue) and watch `/srv/disinto/tape` + the agent log for the push step on branch `fix/issue-1620`.
2. Check compute availability: is VRAM/harness timing out? (see AD-002 llama `--ctx-size` vs concurrent session context sum, AD-002a/AD-002b).
3. Check for harness crashes (exit-code-1, OOM) in the agent container logs.

## What needs verification

- [ ] Is the compute cluster saturated (VRAM/timeout) at the times dev attempts run?
- [ ] Is the harness crashing (OOM / exit-code-1) on these issues, or is it a general compute limit?
- [ ] Is #1620/#1630 the size/class that exceeds the context budget (AD-002b), or a transient cluster-wide limit?
- [ ] Does a fresh run succeed (proving one-off) or deterministically fail (persistent config/compute problem)?

**Decision needed (ops/human):** diagnose the no-push root cause and unblock the dev role so #1620/#1630 can complete, which unblocks #1622/#1631. This is a vault/compute item, not a code task for the dev agent.
